comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers evaluate claims C3, C40-C42 regarding model generation and validation as SUPPORTED. Both cite rigorous experimental evidence including genomic deletion confirmation, cDNA sequencing, and breakpoint analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly describe the evidence as 'convincing, with rigorous biochemical assays.'

Strong agreement. Both evaluate the genotype-phenotype correlation claims (C43-C52) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative grip strength and temporal progression data. Peer reviewers confirm 'pathophysiological changes, including variations in body weight, muscle force, muscle degeneration' with disease progression rates similar to human BMD. Peer review additionally includes C4 and C5 in their evaluation.

Strong agreement with partial overlap. Both evaluate histopathological findings as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on C53-C60, C64 (opaque fibers, necrosis, centronuclear fibers, fibrosis). Peer review covers these plus C61-C63 (comparison with mdx mice). Both cite comprehensive histological data and temporal progression as key evidence.

Strong agreement. Both evaluate molecular characterization claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C65-C70, C74-C75 (dystrophin and nNOS protein levels). Peer review covers these plus C71-C73 (utrophin findings). Both cite immunohistochemistry and Western blot data as rigorous evidence. Peer reviewers describe evidence as 'convincing, with rigorous biochemical assays.'

Agreement on support. OpenEval evaluates C71-C73 (utrophin findings) as SUPPORTED based on Western blot and RT-PCR data. Peer review includes these claims within their broader molecular characterization evaluation (R4), treating them as part of the convincing biochemical evidence distinguishing BMD from mdx models.

Agreement on support. OpenEval evaluates C61-C63 (comparison with mdx mice) as SUPPORTED, noting the characterization as 'minor' is qualitative. Peer review includes these claims in their histopathological evaluation, treating the mdx comparison as supporting evidence for model validity.

Strong agreement. Both evaluate site-specific pathology claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C6, C77-C80 (site-specific vs. diffuse patterns). Peer review covers C6-C7 and C78-C91 (including fiber typing). Both identify this as a novel finding distinguishing BMD from DMD/mdx pathology using state-of-the-art microscopy.

Strong agreement. Both evaluate fiber typing claims (C7, C82-C91) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes selective loss of type IIa fibers with extensive immunohistochemistry data. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as a major strength: 'extensive fiber typing...effectively highlighting a site-specific decline in type IIa muscle fibers in BMD mice.'

Agreement on support. Both evaluate temporal analysis of type IIa fiber loss (C95-C97) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes rigorous time-course data at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Peer review treats this as part of the comprehensive fiber typing characterization supporting the site-specific decline finding.

Agreement on support. Both evaluate CTX injury model findings (C99-C100) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this provides mechanistic context but doesn't fully explain BMD pathology. Peer review implicitly accepts these findings as part of the comprehensive characterization, though they focus more on the overall fiber typing results.

Strong agreement. Both evaluate capillary/vascular findings (C8-C9, C102-C109, C125) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes this as a novel finding with rigorous quantification of endothelial contact area. Peer reviewers acknowledge the 'state-of-the-art microscopy methods' and treat capillary findings as novel observations supporting vascular dysfunction.

Partial agreement. OpenEval evaluates C110, C129 (interconnected capillary branches) as SUPPORTED but notes C129 is speculative and quantification less rigorous. Peer review includes C110 in their broader acceptance of capillary findings (R7) but doesn't specifically address the speculative nature of the interconnection claim.

Disagreement on certainty level. OpenEval evaluates C10, C126-C127, C132 (nNOS-capillary-fiber loss mechanism) as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are explicitly speculative and causality not established. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, treating the mechanistic interpretation as 'reasonable' and 'plausible' without challenging the speculative nature or requesting additional validation.

Partial overlap. OpenEval evaluates C110, C129 as SUPPORTED but with caveats about speculation. Peer review (R8) addresses C10, C126-C127, C129, C132 as SUPPORTED, accepting the vascular dysfunction hypothesis. Both address C129, but peer review is more accepting of the speculative mechanistic claims.

Agreement on uncertainty vs. implicit support. OpenEval evaluates C11, C120 (future utility for therapy) as UNCERTAIN, noting this remains to be demonstrated. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, affirming the models are 'valuable to the field' and 'novel,' implicitly endorsing future research utility without explicitly addressing the speculative nature.

Agreement on support with different groupings. OpenEval evaluates C5, C18-C19, C23-C24 (consistency with human BMD patterns) as SUPPORTED. Peer review includes C5 in their broader phenotypic characterization (R2), confirming 'varying rates of disease progression similar to the human BMD phenotype.' Both validate translational relevance.

OpenEval evaluates C81 (serum CK elevation) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical significance, noting the trend is consistent with muscle damage but weakened by non-significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific claim.

OpenEval evaluates C92-C93 (CSA measurements and fiber type markers) as SUPPORTED, distinguishing type IIa fiber loss from general atrophy. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims, though they may be implicitly included in broader fiber typing acceptance.

OpenEval evaluates C111 (dystrophin structural differences hypothesis) as UNCERTAIN, noting the conclusion is speculative and based on in silico predictions without direct testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific mechanistic claim.

OpenEval evaluates C118 (type IIa fiber loss causing muscle weakness) as UNCERTAIN, noting causality not established despite correlation. Functional studies would be needed for validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific causal claim.
